source: DPROD Contracts dprod-contracts/examples/baseline.ttl, policy <https://example.org/agreements/analytics-customer-2026> (EKGF dprod, develop, 50db943)
needs: dprod:deadline (relative, per-instance PT30M and one P30D)
profile conflict default (odrl:conflict odrl:prohibit on the DPROD profile)
notes: A bilateral DataContract: the obligations are referenced by IRI (duty:cust-*-2026-001) as in the source, and the anonymous permission, prohibition, and second permission are named rule:an-*. The three duty nodes' dprod:dutyState triples (Fulfilled, Active, Active — DPROD's input state Σ) are dropped: due2 derives status from evidence and activation, and where Σ would have been produced from the same evidence the two agree (due2-profiles.md §8.2 exception 2). Bilateral shape: duty:cust-delivery and duty:cust-schema name the data platform as subjectOfDuty (grantorDuties), duty:cust-report names analytics (granteeDuties); each also names objectOfDuty, which is metadata for matching in DPROD and plays no role in due2's witness test (the bearer performs, due2-workflows.md §5.3). Every rule of this contract states its own assignee, so DPROD's Agreement-party reading (§7.3: either party of the agreement makes the policy applicable) does not widen any rule: a grantor request is NotApplicable in both systems, and the exception-4 divergence (subject-less rules) is not exercised here — dprod-divergences covers it. DPROD duty collection (§7.2 step 1): deliver, conformTo, and report never match read, distribute, or derive, so no duty is ever collected and no violation denies. Intended §7.4 reading throughout.

scenarios.name: analytics reads, yesterday delivered, today still open

expected.why: rule:an-read applies (assignee analytics, read, customer-data) and the distribute prohibition does not match read: Permit. Anchored at 2026-02-09T07:00, the daily delivery yields two occurrences ≤ effective_at: 02-09, witnessed at 07:10 within its window (fulfilled), and 02-10, whose window runs to 07:30 (outstanding). The schema conformance has no deadline and no witness: outstanding. The report duty has no activation entry, so its P30D runs from effective_at: outstanding.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (the agreement is applicable for the grantee, the permission is active, and no duty is collected for a read)

scenarios.name: the grantor reads under its own contract

expected.why: The data platform is the assigner, and no rule of this contract reaches it: both permissions and the prohibition name analytics as assignee, and the request party is not below analytics in any declared party closure. No rule matches, so the contract does not govern the grantor's own read: NotApplicable, and no obligation is in force (in force needs a Permit or Forbid of the policy to match). DPROD agrees: the agreement is applicable (the agent is a party, §7.3), but every norm's subject is analytics, so nothing is active.

scenarios.dprod_expected: NotApplicable (applicable agreement, but no norm is active for the grantor — every rule names the grantee)

expected.why: rule:an-no-distribute matches by equality and assignee: Deny. The schema obligation is in force — a Forbid of the policy matches the request, which is what in force turns on — and outstanding.

scenarios.name: overdue usage report under DPROD-faithful deny

expected.why: The report duty was activated on 2026-01-05 (the case history supplies it), so its P30D deadline passed on 2026-02-04; with no witness by effective_at 2026-02-10 it is violated, and under violations = deny that denies the grantee's read — the consumer is held to its own reporting duty. The delivery duty has no activation entry, so its anchor is effective_at 07:10, which the daily-07:00 rule does not generate: no instance is owed yet, and an obligation with no owed instance is not reported (not-yet-owed, due2-profiles.md §9). The schema obligation is in force and outstanding.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (report never matches read, so the duty is not collected and the violation never denies — exception 6)
